prize_parts.citation: for showing how firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting shape trade patterns and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: Firm heterogeneity and selection moved trade analysis from countries and industries to firms. Melitz (2003) is a clear originating model. It identifies a reallocation channel for gains from trade, and Helpman's wider programme, including the work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, supports his credit. Two decades of firm-level data work have tested the framework, and it is now the standard way trade is modelled and measured. That record of testing matters to me because I weight work that has been confronted with micro and register data. Compared with my opening first choice, B019, the attribution here is much cleaner. Eight names are credited on B019 and any three-person selection leaves out major contributors. I still regard the New Keynesian framework as highly influential. I no longer think I can recommend a three-name award for it at this stage.
statement.case_against: Priority and credit are not fully settled. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum made closely related empirical and theoretical contributions that are not credited on this entry. Krugman's 2008 prize covered the earlier monopolistic-competition trade framework on which this work builds. Some welfare conclusions depend on functional-form assumptions, such as the way selection and productivity distributions are specified. Helpman's contributions also appear in another trade entry, so the scope of his credit needs delimiting.

responses.point: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) originated the collateral-constraint amplification mechanism. The paper is nearly three decades old and was tested during the 2007-09 crisis. Limiting credit to the two originators keeps attribution clean, and the 2022 prize covered adjacent but distinct ground.
responses.response: I agree that attribution is cleaner for B011 than for the other macro entries, and that the maturity argument is strong. I keep it as an alternative for that reason. I qualify the claim that the crisis confirmed the mechanism. The collateral channel is hard to identify directly, and the quantitative size of the amplification is not pinned down by the episodes cited. A credit-cycle model that is conceptually foundational but weakly identified is, to me, a somewhat different kind of achievement from one with a long record of firm-level testing. The 2022 overlap also weighs more heavily with me than your opening allows.

responses.point: Melitz is the central originator and Helpman has foundational credit, while Redding is more derivative of the core insight. Bernard, Eaton, Kortum and Jensen made closely related contributions that are not credited on the entry, so priority may be contested.
responses.response: I agree with the two-name core and with leaving Redding out. I do not think the omitted names should be waved away, because they are the main threat to the citation. The way to handle it is to word the citation around the heterogeneous-firm selection model and its welfare implications, which is where Melitz's contribution is distinctive. It should not claim the whole empirical firm-trade literature. I also accept your point about severe attribution difficulty on B019. That is why I have moved away from my opening first choice.

responses.point: B012 is a coherent field-founding contribution. Persson, Tabellini and Besley form a natural trio, and the area is adjacent to the 2024 institutions prize without duplicating it.
responses.response: I agree that this is the cleanest three-name attribution on the shortlist, which is why I ranked it second and keep it as an alternative. I am less sure that the 2024 overlap can be set aside as easily as the opening suggests. The cross-country evidence on constitutional and electoral rules is also harder to identify than the formal theory. That is the main reason I place it behind B005, where the central mechanism has been tested more directly against micro data. I note Per Strömberg's remark that Persson's past committee role may raise a conflict question. The protocol discloses but does not adjudicate such connections, and I leave it there.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can word a citation for B005 that does not overreach on the contributions of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum.
How much of the Helpman credit overlaps with Krugman's 2008 prize and with his separate trade entry.
How sensitive the welfare conclusions are to functional-form assumptions.
Whether the attribution problem on B019 can be resolved by a defensible three-name selection. If it can, I would revisit my opening ranking.
My assessments rely on prior knowledge and on the supplied committee text. I have not independently verified any source.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The listed co-authors (Holmlund, Edin, Åslund, Öckert, Johansson, Nybom, Oosterbeek, van Ours) are not credited on any shortlisted entry. The Stockholm University overlap with the IIES macro group (Hassler, Krusell) is an institutional overlap with fellow members, not a link to a candidate.
